records.rejectedPreview:
A fictional survey by Elena Ruiz included 240 respondents from three offices. Employees who reported having a quiet workspace also reported fewer interruptions; however, this association does not establish that quiet workspaces caused the difference, and the survey did not measure productivity.

Among respondents, 38% preferred working remotely, 42% preferred a hybrid arrangement, and 20% preferred working in the office. These preferences describe the sample rather than the wider workforce, and because participation was voluntary, selection bias may have affected the results.

The report states, "The results are preliminary and should not guide staffing decisions." A follow-up survey could help determine whether preferences change over time, but it would not, by itself, establish causation. Ultimately, the findings offer a limited description of this sample rather than proof that one working arrangement is superior.
